ci95_type: clip-grouped bootstrap of the median over 12 windows (2000 draws, seed 0) -- but all windows come from ONE clip, so this interval reflects window-to-window spread only, not clip-to-clip spread. shipped_norm: [348.44840599544114, 348.44840599544114], shipped_raw: [330.33776550291805, 330.33776550291805]

config.source: 480p IndEgo clip, 10 fps native, 30 fps normalisation pre-pass for the shipped arm

confounds: Same laptop, same session; other desktop load was present (no isolation, no cpu pinning) -- the medians describe this machine, they are not a bound.
All timed windows come from ONE IndEgo clip, so clip-to-clip variation is not sampled; the interval covers window spread only.

The shipped arm decodes the 30 fps-normalised file that the portal creates (the pre-pass itself is reported separately); the raw arm decodes the 10 fps source and frame-repeats, and both arms then pay for the same 300-frame buffer.
The shipped arm's decode is ffmpeg to 160x90, the mosaic arm's is cv2 at 480p: this compares front ends as each path actually pays them, not two encoders on equal work.
feature_vector includes the diff group (the S1 harness configuration); the GRID.05 S0 parity probe needs spatial+intertile only and is cheaper.
CRF 18 libx264 for the normalisation pre-pass: a different encoder setting moves that one-off number, not the per-window numbers.
cost: 36 shipped-normalised + 36 shipped-raw + 36 mosaic passes + 36 cv2 decodes single-process, then 72 jobs on 2 workers; wall 13.7 s
device: CPU only (this laptop, 22 cores / 15 GB RAM; GPU not used)

footage_hours_per_wall_hour.formula: 10000 / median_total_ms (10 s of footage per window, no idle)

measured_2_worker_aggregate.note: mixed job stream (half shipped, half mosaic) with two real worker processes; it is the measured throughput of that mix, not a per-path number

measured_2_worker_pure_mosaic.note: mosaic-only job stream, two worker processes.  Compare with mosaic_1_worker: the per-job median RISES under two workers, so throughput does not double on this laptop.

label_source: no labels involved: cost only. Windows are real IndEgo 480p footage (read-only, no frames committed)
n_note: n = timed window passes per arm (12 windows x 3 repeats); n_bad is 0 because this experiment measures cost, not detection

normalisation_pre_pass.note: one-off per clip, NOT included in any per-window number above; the portal writes normalised_30fps.mp4 once per input file

not_measured: No GPU number, no cross-device claim, no Raspberry Pi or other edge board.
No thermal soak, no multi-hour run, no service overhead (upload, container, receipt write, PNG encode of the canvas).
No measurement of the memory footprint or of disk I/O.
protocol: 12 human-good IndEgo windows from ONE clip x 3 repeats, single process, every stage timed in-process; plus a measured 2-worker aggregate run. CPU only, 480p source, 10 s windows, nice -n 10, OMP_NUM_THREADS=2

worker_scaling.note: measured ratio, same laptop and session: the second worker buys less than 2x because the per-job time itself rises
